PRE-TECHNICAL STUDIES — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #7
====

GRADE: Grade 7
SUBJECT: PRE-TECHNICAL STUDIES
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KJSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Before using a sharp tool in a workshop, you should: (1 mark)
   A. Run with the tool
   B. Work alone with eyes closed
   C. Remove all guards
   D. Wear safety gear and follow instructions

2. When learning Introduction to Pre-Technical Studies, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Introduction to Pre-Technical Studies.
   B. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Introduction to Pre-Technical Studies.
   C. Skip safety briefings for Introduction to Pre-Technical Studies.
   D. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Introduction to Pre-Technical Studies.

3. When learning Computer Concepts, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Computer Concepts.
   B. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Computer Concepts.
   C. Skip safety briefings for Computer Concepts.
   D. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Computer Concepts.

4. When learning Introduction to Materials, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Introduction to Materials.
   B. Skip safety briefings for Introduction to Materials.
   C. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Introduction to Materials.
   D. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Introduction to Materials.

5. When learning Non- Metallic Materials, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Non- Metallic Materials.
   B. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Non- Metallic Materials.
   C. Skip safety briefings for Non- Metallic Materials.
   D. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Non- Metallic Materials.

6. When learning Metallic Materials, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Metallic Materials.
   B. Skip safety briefings for Metallic Materials.
   C. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Metallic Materials.
   D. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Metallic Materials.

7. ICT stands for: (1 mark)
   A. Internal Cooking Timer
   B. International Cricket Team
   C. Input Cable Tester
   D. Information and Communication Technology

8. When learning Safety in the Immediate Environment, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Safety in the Immediate Environment.
   B. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Safety in the Immediate Environment.
   C. Skip safety briefings for Safety in the Immediate Environment.
   D. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Safety in the Immediate Environment.

9. A computer’s main brain for processing is the: (1 mark)
   A. CPU
   B. Monitor
   C. Keyboard
   D. Speaker

10. Electricity safety rule: (1 mark)
   A. Overload every socket
   B. Ignore burnt cables
   C. Insert metal objects into sockets for fun
   D. Never touch live wires with wet hands

11. When learning Measuring and Marking Out Tools, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Skip safety briefings for Measuring and Marking Out Tools.
   B. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Measuring and Marking Out Tools.
   C. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Measuring and Marking Out Tools.
   D. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Measuring and Marking Out Tools.

12. When learning ICT Tools in Communication, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Guess wiring or cutting steps for ICT Tools in Communication.
   B. Leave sharp tools on the floor after ICT Tools in Communication.
   C. Skip safety briefings for ICT Tools in Communication.
   D. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for ICT Tools in Communication.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Computer Hardware and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Introduction to Entrepreneurship 8 5.2 Production Unit 10 5.3 Financial Goals 10 and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Introduction to Entrepreneurship and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Production Unit 10 5.3 Financial Goals 10 Total Number of Lessons 120 Note: The  and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MARKING SCHEME
====

1. D — Wear safety gear and follow instructions

2. B — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Introduction to Pre-Technical Studies.

3. B — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Computer Concepts.

4. D — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Introduction to Materials.

5. D — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Non- Metallic Materials.

6. D — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Metallic Materials.

7. D — Information and Communication Technology

8. D — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Safety in the Immediate Environment.

9. A — CPU

10. D — Never touch live wires with wet hands

11. C — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Measuring and Marking Out Tools.

12. D — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for ICT Tools in Communication.

13. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Computer Hardware; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Introduction to Entrepreneurship; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Production Unit 10 5.3 Financial Goals 10 Total Number of Lessons 120 Note: The ; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
